blocks.content: Cultural questions on A&N typically focus on the syncretic, migrant-shaped culture of the settler population and the traditional practices of the Nicobarese (since the more isolated tribes have limited documented 'festival' culture accessible to outsiders).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India's linguistic diversity forms a core component of its cultural identity.
Festivals celebrate regional traditions, seasonal cycles, and historical legacies.
Handicrafts and traditional practices showcase local artistic craftsmanship and heritage.
Heritage sites and museums preserve tangible historical artifacts and architectural monuments.
No single indigenous majority language — Hindi and Bengali are the most widely spoken among settlers, alongside Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Nicobarese/Car dialects among the Nicobarese.

The Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa and Sentinelese languages form the Andamanese/Great Andamanese language family — considered linguistically unique and unrelated to any mainland Indian language family, a subject of major interest to linguists (many now extinct or critically endangered).
The Shompen and Nicobarese languages belong to the Austroasiatic (Mon-Khmer) language family, linking them linguistically to Southeast Asia rather than mainland India.

items: Handicrafts: shell-craft and coral-craft items (now regulated/discouraged for environmental reasons), coconut-shell craft, cane and bamboo work, and wood carving are traditional local crafts sold as tourist souvenirs.
Traditional Nicobarese houses are built on stilts (to protect against flooding and pests), typically circular or oval in plan with thatched conical roofs — an architectural fact occasionally tested.
Seafood dominates the local cuisine given the maritime setting; coconut is used extensively in cooking across both settler and tribal communities.

The Anthropological Survey of India and the A&N Tribal Welfare Department maintain museums and documentation centres — notably the Anthropological Museum, Port Blair, and the Samudrika Naval Marine Museum.
UNESCO World Heritage Sites and Classical Languages are high-frequency exam topics.
GI tags related to traditional handicrafts and regional cuisines are regularly tested in prelims.
Questions frequently pair regional festivals and traditional art forms with their respective states.

items: No single native majority language; Hindi/Bengali dominant among settlers; Andamanese and Nicobarese/Shompen languages belong to two entirely different, non-mainland-Indian language families.
Island Tourism Festival — flagship annual cultural/tourism event of the UT government, held in Port Blair.

Samudrika Naval Marine Museum and the Anthropological Museum are the key heritage museums of Port Blair.
